reading.rtitle: Plan, Stay Calm, and Keep Every Receipt
paras: Two years ago, I used to hate business trips. I used to pack the night before and hope for the best. Then my company sent me to a trade fair in Germany, and I learned to plan. Now, a week before every trip, I print my itinerary and check my baggage allowance on the airline website, because an extra bag at the airport always costs more.

On that first trip, I had a three-hour layover in Frankfurt, and my connection was canceled. The gate agent said that the next flight was at nine p.m., and she gave me a voucher for dinner. I was tired, but I stayed calm. At the hotel, the room next to mine was very loud at midnight, so I called the front desk and made a polite noise complaint. They moved me to a quiet room, and breakfast the next morning was complimentary.

The fair itself was the easy part. Before my first meeting, I made small talk with a supplier about a famous landmark in the city, and the meeting went very well. On my last day, I asked for a late checkout, because my flight was in the evening. And one more tip: always ask for a receipt. Without it, my company can't pay me back. Today, when a younger colleague travels for the first time, I tell her: plan, stay calm, and keep every receipt.

listenings.text: Attention, please. Passengers on Flight seventy-seven twenty to Lyon: this flight is delayed by two hours because of bad weather in Lyon. The new departure time is four o'clock. If you have a meeting this afternoon, please speak to an agent at gate twelve. We will be giving each passenger a voucher for a meal at any restaurant in the terminal. If the weather does not improve, we will rebook you on the evening train to Lyon at no cost. Please keep your boarding pass, and keep the receipt for any extra costs. We apologize for the inconvenience, and we will be updating this information every thirty minutes.

Hello, Ms. Ito. This is Claire from the front desk of your hotel in Lyon. I am calling about your stay from November thirteen to sixteen. First, the airline called us about a delay, so you must be arriving late tonight. Don't worry: we will be keeping your room until midnight. Second, you asked to have your suit pressed. We will have it ready on Thursday by seven a.m. Third, your flight home is on Sunday evening, so we can give you a late checkout, until two p.m. It is complimentary for our business guests. If you need anything else, just call the front desk. Have a safe trip, and see you soon!

extra_audio.text: First, I print my itinerary and check my baggage allowance. Then, at the airport, I check my bag and go through security. Next, I have a short layover in Paris before my flight to Lyon. After that, I check in at the hotel and have my suit pressed. Finally, I ask for a late checkout and keep every receipt.
